newsitem.title: USA: High techs stumble, pressure Nasdaq.
newsitem.headline: High techs stumble, pressure Nasdaq.

text.p: Nasdaq shares dropped Tuesday as large capitalization technology took a beating after two industry leaders warned their quarterly results will fall short of expectations, traders said.
The Nasdaq composite index lost 19.88 points or 1.42 percent to 1384.91. Declining issues beat gaining issues on a ratio of about 11 to 10 on total volume of 597 million shares.

"You got the high techs, everything, closing on their lows. It kind of got ugly the last part of the day. It was a definitely a day when everything was overshadowed by the high techs," said Nicholas Karos, senior over-the-counter trader with Piper Jaffray.

Traders said the low share prices failed to attract even bargain hunting investors. "People want to wait until the dust settles to see if the problems are just connected to a few companies," another trader said.
Disk drive makers and networking companies were among the hardest hit by Seagate Technology Inc's and Cabletron Systems Inc's earnings warning, traders said.
Of the 25 most-active Nasdaq issues, only RF Micro Devices Inc, which launched it initial public offering, saw a gain. RF Micro added 3-5/16 to its offering price of 12.
